glossary.meaning: a narrator who tells the story as I, from inside it

memorial: Something built to keep a memory standing.
inscription: It starts with in and has script in the middle.
description: Writing that shows what something is like.

miss.even: Say e-ven. The first beat, e, ends on the vowel e, and the e says its name. That makes it open.
miss.river: Say riv-er. The first beat, riv, ends on the consonant v, and the i is short. That makes it closed.
miss.moment: Say mo-ment. The first beat, mo, ends on the vowel o, and the o says its name. That makes it open.
miss.shiver: Say shiv-er. The first beat, shiv, ends on the consonant v, and the i is short. That makes it closed.
miss.silent: Say si-lent. The first beat, si, ends on the vowel i, and the i says its name. That makes it open.
miss.visit: Say vis-it. The first beat, vis, ends on the consonant s, and the i is short. That makes it closed.
miss.final: Say fi-nal. The first beat, fi, ends on the vowel i, and the i says its name. That makes it open.
miss.never: Say nev-er. The first beat, nev, ends on the consonant v, and the e is short. That makes it closed.

art.title: Ball-play of the Choctaw: Ball Up
art.alt: A painting of a huge stickball game on a green field, with hundreds of Choctaw players running and reaching with sticks.
art.look: George Catlin painted this stickball game in 1834–35. He watched it in 1834 in Indian Territory, now Oklahoma, after many Choctaw families had already been forced to move west. Stickball was, and still is, an important Choctaw game. Luke runs off to play it in Chapter 2. Even in hard times, people still play.
art.creator: George Catlin
art.lookBtn: Tap to learn about this stickball painting

checks.q: Jumper talks in this book. Does that mean the history in it is made up?

options.t: Yes. A talking dog means none of it is real.
options.why: How I Became a Ghost is historical fiction: a made-up story, with a talking dog and a ghost, set inside real history. The treaty that took the Choctaw homeland in Mississippi was real, and it was signed in 1830.

options.t: No. The story is made up, but the history around it is real.
options.why: That is historical fiction: a made-up story set inside real history. The treaty that took the Choctaw homeland in Mississippi was real, and it was signed in 1830.
